title: Finite chart models and etale localization of logarithmic differentials
statement:
Let $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], whose underlying scheme map is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Define $\omega_f$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] by sheafifying [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] the $\mathcal O_X$-module on symbols $da$ for functions and $d\log m$ for log sections, with relations: $d$ is additive, $d(ab)=a\,db+b\,da$, $d\log(mm')=d\log m+d\log m'$, $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$, and $dc=d\log n=0$ for functions and log sections pulled back from $Y$.

Every geometric point [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] has a pointed etale neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ mapping to an affine etale neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$, with pulled-back log structures and a chart $P\to M|_U$ by a finitely generated integral monoid, and a finitely presented $A$-module $W$ such that $\omega_{U/V}(\operatorname{Spec}B)\cong B\otimes_AW$ for every affine etale $\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$. Here finitely presented means the cokernel of a map $A^u\to A^v$ for finite $u,v$. These isomorphisms respect restriction, scalar multiplication, and the symbols $da,d\log m$; thus they identify $\omega_{U/V}$ with the module sheaf given by this tensor formula.

More generally, for any commutative square $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:X'\to X$, $h:Y'\to Y$, $hf'=fg$, where $g,h$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and both log structures are pulled back, the canonical map $g^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$ is an isomorphism. Its formulas are $1\otimes da\mapsto d(g^\sharp a)$ and $1\otimes d\log m\mapsto d\log(g^\flat m)$. Here $g^*\omega_f=\mathcal O_{X'}\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_X}g^{-1}\omega_f$. No infinitesimal lifting or smoothness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof, printed p.252 (log differential sheaf). Precise general input: Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie, 1.7, 2.1 and chart discussion 2.9, printed pp.195--200; WANTED locally, primary source read online. Etale localization uses the ordinary formally etale differential comparison.

proof.text: First record an ordinary etale calculation that will be used below. If $R\to A\to B$ are ring maps with $A\to B$ etale, and $H$ is any $B$-module, restriction gives a bijection $\operatorname{Der}_R(B,H)\to\operatorname{Der}_R(A,H)$. Indeed form the ring $B\oplus H$ with $(b,h)(b',h')=(bb',bh'+b'h)$, square-zero ideal $0\oplus H$, and $A$-structure $a\mapsto(\bar a,D(a))$. The unique infinitesimal lifting property of the etale map gives a unique $A$-map $B\to B\oplus H$ lifting $\mathrm{id}_B$. It has the form $b\mapsto(b,\widetilde D(b))$, and the ring-map equations say exactly that $\widetilde D$ is an $R$-derivation extending $D$. The cited lifting theorem applies because etale implies flat and unramified; it requires no Noetherian condition on the test ring. In particular derivations over an etale base vanish. If also $R\to R'$ is etale and $R'\to B$ is compatible, every extended $R$-derivation of $B$ kills $R'$: its restriction to $R'$ and zero are the two lifts of the zero derivation on $R$, hence agree.

source.place: Definition 02HG (definition-formally-etale); square-zero calculation from the unique-lifting statement of lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$. By the definition of an fs log scheme choose an affine pointed etale chart neighbourhood $V\to Y$ of $f(\bar x)$ with chart $Q$, and a pointed etale chart neighbourhood of $\bar x$ over $X\times_Y V$ with chart $P$. The fibre-product point is the pair of the chosen lifts. Etale base change and composition ensure that the latter neighbourhood is etale over $X$. These charts may be refined by affine opens. Both $P$ and $Q$ are finitely generated integral monoids. All log structures in these choices are the pulled-back ones. Every map here is a scheme morphism, hence representable by algebraic spaces over $Y$; thus the current representability hypothesis of the cited calculus holds.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1--1.2, charts of fine log structures; explicit neighbourhood refinement below the chart discussion used in XVI 3.6.3

proof.text: Choose monoid generators $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $Q$ and write $m_i=f^\flat(q_i)$ on the source chart neighbourhood. The associated-log description says that the germ of each $m_i$ has the form $[v_i,u_i]$ with $v_i\in P$ and $u_i$ an invertible function germ. The stalk colimit and cofilteredness let us lift these finitely many units and equalities simultaneously to one pointed etale refinement. Equivalently the local-section description of sheafification gives representatives $m_i=[v_i,u_i]$ there. Shrink further so all $u_i$ remain units. We do not assert a homomorphism $Q\to P$ or select compatible lifts of the relations of $Q$; only the finitely many displayed log sections are used.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1--1.2, associated log structure and chart pushout; simultaneous refinement by the geometric-stalk definition

proof.text: After these refinements the underlying map to $V$ is locally of finite presentation, by the base-change and composition calculus and the fact that etale morphisms are locally of finite presentation. Its definition allows us to replace the two neighbourhoods by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_l)$. All previously chosen charts and identities restrict to these opens. The source $U$ is locally Noetherian: $U\to X$ is etale, hence locally of finite type, and $X$ is locally Noetherian. Therefore $A$ is Noetherian by the affine-open theorem, applied to the whole of $U$. This is the only use of Noetherianity below.

source.place: Local finite presentation and locally Noetherian sources; apply the cited definitions and permanence statements after chart refinement

proof.text:
Let $\beta:P\to A$ be the source chart, and let $[p]\in P^{\rm gp}$ denote the class of $p$. Form
$$E=\Omega_{A/R}\oplus(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}P^{\rm gp}).$$
Write $\lambda_p=(0,1\otimes[p])$. Define $W$ as the quotient of $E$ by the $A$-submodule generated by
$$(d\beta(p),0)-\beta(p)\lambda_p\quad(p\in P),\qquad (u_i^{-1}du_i,0)+\lambda_{v_i}\quad(1\le i\le s).$$
We use the same notation for the images of $da$ and $\lambda_p$ in $W$. Thus the construction imposes the source structural relations and kills the chosen generators of the base log structure. It does not use a lifting or smoothness hypothesis.

source.place: Explicit chart quotient derived from the defining log-differential relations; agent calculation supplementing XVI 3.6.3

proof.text: The Leibniz and additivity relations show that $\Omega_{A/R}$ is generated by $dx_1,\ldots,dx_n$: differentiate a polynomial expression for any $a\in A$, with $dr=0$ for $r\in R$. If $p_1,\ldots,p_t$ generate $P$, then their classes generate $P^{\rm gp}$ as an abelian group, so the $\lambda_{p_j}$ generate $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}P^{\rm gp}$. Consequently $W$ is generated by the images of these $n+t$ elements. The cited Noetherian finite-module theorem now gives a finite presentation $A^u\to A^v\to W\to0$. There is no need to claim that the displayed possibly infinite set of structural relations itself is finite, nor to assume $P^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free.

source.place: Finite generation from the universal differential relations; Noetherian finite presentation (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation, part (1))

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal H=(\widetilde W)_{\rm et}$. The affine associated-module theorem supplies the quasi-coherent sheaf $\widetilde W$ with $\Gamma(U,\widetilde W)=W$ (take the principal open $D(1)$). Quasi-coherent etale descent makes $T\mapsto\Gamma(T,t^*\widetilde W)$ a sheaf on $U_{\rm et}$. For every affine etale $t:T=\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$, affine pullback sections give
$$\mathcal H(T)=B\otimes_AW,$$
with the map on a pure tensor equal to multiplication by $b$ of the pulled-back section $w$. These identifications are natural in $W$. Restrictions between affine objects are $b\otimes w\mapsto\rho(b)\otimes w$: the pullback of a section pulled back from $U$ is its pullback along the composite, and the scalar action restricts by $\rho$.

source.place: lemma-spec-sheaves and Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback); etale sheaf descent as stated in lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent

proof.text: For an affine etale $T=\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$, extend the derivation $A\to B\otimes_AW$, $a\mapsto1\otimes da$, uniquely to an $R$-derivation $D_B:B\to B\otimes_AW$ using step 1. For a map of affine etale $U$-objects with ring map $B\to C$, the two derivations from $B$ to $C\otimes_AW$ obtained by restricting $D_C$ or extending scalars in $D_B$ agree on $A$, hence agree by step 1. Thus these are a derivation of sheaves $D:\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal H$, with the analogous formula on nonaffine objects obtained by gluing on affine opens.

source.place: Application of the etale extension calculation of step 1, with the universal derivation into the explicitly constructed quotient

proof.text:
On a local representative $[p,u]$ of the source associated log structure define
$$\delta([p,u])=1\otimes\lambda_p+u^{-1}D(u).$$
This is well defined on its pushout: for $e$ with $\beta(e)$ a unit, the relation in $W$ gives $1\otimes\lambda_e=\beta(e)^{-1}D(\beta(e))$, so the representatives $[pe,u]$ and $[p,\beta(e)u]$ have the same value. The Leibniz rule gives $(uv)^{-1}D(uv)=u^{-1}D(u)+v^{-1}D(v)$, hence additivity under monoid multiplication. Also
$$D(\beta(p)u)=\beta(p)u\bigl(1\otimes\lambda_p+u^{-1}D(u)\bigr).$$
The associated-log node identifies $M|_U$ with the sheafification of these pushouts. The displayed maps respect restrictions, so sheafification extends them uniquely to $\delta:M|_U\to\mathcal H$ satisfying $D\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)\delta(m)$. In particular the calculation proves the extension across logification rather than invoking an unnamed log-differential comparison theorem.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1--1.2 associated-log pushout, explicit derivation calculation; the quotient relations are those suggested by the log differential in XVI 3.6.3

proof.text: The pair $(D,\delta)$ kills the base ring and base log sections, including those defined only etale locally on $V$. Indeed any such function is locally on an affine etale $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to V$; its pullback has derivative zero by the last assertion of step 1. Any base log section is etale locally $[q,c]$ in the associated-log chart $Q$, with $c$ a unit of such an $R'$. Since $q$ is a product of the $q_i$, its image has $\delta$ equal to the sum of the $\delta(m_i)$, each zero by the second family of relations defining $W$. The unit contributes $c^{-1}D(c)=0$. Local representatives suffice because the target $\mathcal H$ is a sheaf. This checks all base relations, not just the global functions in $R$ or the selected $q_i$.

source.place: Explicit verification of all base relations for the chart quotient, including etale-local base functions and units

proof.text: Send each differential symbol $db$ to $D(b)$ and each log symbol $d\log m$ to $\delta(m)$. Steps 8--10 verify additivity, Leibniz, monoid additivity, the structural relation and all base relations. The maps commute with restrictions, so the universal property of sheafification gives a map $\Phi:\omega_{U/V}\to\mathcal H$. Conversely send $da\in W$ to the differential of $a$ in $\omega_{U/V}(U)$ and $\lambda_p$ to $d\log p$. The universal property of $\Omega_{A/R}$ supplies the first summand's map. The defining relations of $W$ hold in $\omega_{U/V}$; for the second family use $d\log m_i=0$ and $d\log u_i=u_i^{-1}du_i$. This gives $W\to\omega_{U/V}(U)$. On affine etale $T$ extend it by $b\otimes w\mapsto b\,w|_T$. The tensor restriction formula in step 7 makes these maps compatible; affine cover density and the sheaf gluing axiom extend them uniquely to $\Psi:\mathcal H\to\omega_{U/V}$.

source.place: Construction of the two comparison maps from the symbol relations; agent proof supplementing the log-differential use in XVI 3.6.3

proof.text: The composite $\Phi\Psi$ fixes $1\otimes da$ and $1\otimes\lambda_p$, hence every $b\otimes w$. For $\Psi\Phi$, the induced derivation on an affine etale $B$ with values in $\omega_{U/V}(\operatorname{Spec}B)$ agrees with $b\mapsto db$ on $A$; uniqueness in step 1 makes it agree on every $b\in B$. On a log representative $[p,u]$ it gives $d\log p+u^{-1}du=d\log[p,u]$, since $du=u\,d\log u$ for a unit. Local representatives and sheaf gluing give equality on every log symbol. The composites are therefore identities. Hence $\omega_{U/V}\simeq\mathcal H$ on the entire small etale site, with affine sections $B\otimes_AW$ and the required scalar, restriction and symbol formulas.

source.place: Verification of the inverse maps on functions and associated-log representatives; no smoothness assumption

proof.text: We also check that the chart computation calculates the restriction of the original $\omega_f$. For the etale map $j:U\to X$, the inverse-image restriction theorem identifies $j^{-1}\omega_f$ with $\omega_f|_U$. The same restriction identifies $j^{-1}\mathcal O_X$ with $\mathcal O_U$, since on $T\to U$ both assign $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$; hence the tensor formula gives $j^*\omega_f=\omega_f|_U$. The etale slice equivalence identifies the local source symbols with those on $U_{\rm et}$. Restriction of their sheafification has the same local generators and relations: sections of a sheafification are locally represented, and equality of two representatives is local, by the cited local-section theorem. The maps and inverse check of steps 8--12 thus work for $\omega_f|_U$ as well. Here $R$ and the $q_i$ already define base symbols through the etale object $V\to Y$. For any other base symbol on an etale $Z\to Y$, pull back along $Z\times_YV\to V$ and refine by affine opens; this is etale over $V$, so step 10 kills that symbol too. Therefore the canonical identifications are $j^*\omega_f\simeq\omega_{U/V}\simeq\mathcal H$.

source.place: Section 03S2 (section-extension-by-zero), inverse image is restriction; Sites Section 00XZ (section-localize); local representatives and equalities in sheafification as quoted in lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local

proof.text: Now take the general square in the statement. Etale locally on $X'$ and $Y'$ refine the above chart neighbourhoods to affine compatible neighbourhoods $U'=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ mapping to $U$ and $V$, with $A\to B$ and $R\to R'$ etale. Explicitly choose an affine pointed refinement $V'$ of $Y'\times_YV$, then an affine pointed refinement $U'$ of $X'\times_{Y'}V'\times_{X\times_YV}U$. The map to $U$ is etale: before the open refinements it is a composite of base changes of $g$ and $V'\to V$. Thus both ring maps are etale. Because the log structures are pulled back, $P$ and $Q$ remain charts and the base log generators are still $[v_i,u_i|_{U'}]$. Step 1 gives a bijection between $R'$-derivations of $B$ and $R$-derivations of $A$ with values in any $B$-module: extension along $A\to B$ is unique, and it kills $R'$ by etaleness of $R\to R'$. For the log part the formula in step 9 adjoins precisely the new units, with their forced values $u^{-1}D(u)$. If $\beta(p)$ becomes a unit only in $B$, the scalar-extended structural relation forces $\lambda_p=\beta(p)^{-1}D(\beta(p))$, so logification still respects that relation. For any $B$-module $H$, a map $B\otimes_AW\to H$ is exactly an $R$-derivation of $A$ and an additive map $P^{\rm gp}\to H$ satisfying the two relation families of step 5. Extend the derivation uniquely to $B$ and extend the log map by the unit formula of step 9; these satisfy all $R'$ and base-log relations by step 10. Conversely restriction recovers the two maps and their relations. The extensions are unique and inverse to restriction. Thus the same quotient relations as in step 5, extended to $B$, give the symbol sheaf for $U'/V'$; the explicit inverse-map verification in steps 8--12 applies unchanged and identifies it with $(\widetilde{B\otimes_AW})_{\rm et}$. This argument does not assume that the square is cartesian.

source.place: Etale localization of the symbol construction: source and base derivation comparisons and the associated-log unit formula, proved explicitly

proof.text: The quasi-coherent change-of-topology comparison identifies the ringed-etale tensor pullback of $(\widetilde W)_{\rm et}$ with the etale sheaf associated to the ordinary module pullback of $\widetilde W$. Affine tilde pullback identifies the latter with $(\widetilde{B\otimes_AW})_{\rm et}$. Combined with steps 13--14 this makes the canonical map $g^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$ an isomorphism on the chosen neighbourhoods. It is the canonical map because its effect is $1\otimes da\mapsto d(g^\sharp a)$ and $1\otimes d\log m\mapsto d\log(g^\flat m)$. The same formulas hold on overlaps and determine the maps on local symbol generators, so the local inverses agree on overlaps and glue uniquely to a global inverse. This also shows that every identification respects scalar multiplication and restriction, and completes both assertions.

tool_uses.why: Ordinary etale maps have unique square-zero lifts; used only to extend ordinary derivations, not as a logarithmic lifting assumption.
The associated-log chart is the sheafification of the explicit monoid-unit pushout; the unit route has no substitute for this construction.
Represent log sections by chart elements and units etale locally; this is the sheafification tool rather than a cohomological route.
Take one common pointed refinement for finitely many base-chart generator representatives.
Refine pointed etale chart neighbourhoods by affine ones.
An etale neighbourhood of the locally Noetherian source is locally Noetherian.
The coordinate ring of the chosen affine locally Noetherian source is Noetherian.
The associated quasi-coherent tensor formula is already a sheaf on the small etale site.
Computes that sheaf on affine etale objects as B tensor W, with the normalized section formula.
Compares ordinary and ringed-etale tensor pullback of the model sheaf; no log-theoretic conclusion is taken from it.
Pulls the associated module W to the associated scalar-extended module on an affine source.
Computes etale inverse image as restriction; the ringed tensor pullback then collapses because the restricted structure sheaf is unchanged.
Identifies the small etale site of a chart neighbourhood with the slice, so the local symbol constructions can be compared.
Refines arbitrary etale base symbols to fibre products with the chosen chart without imposing a cartesian hypothesis on f itself.
